data.name: Rhianna
data.gender_notes: Rhianna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Welsh roots ‘rhi’ (river) and ‘anna’ (graceful, lovely, radiant). The name symbolizes a beautiful and powerful stream, reminding us of God’s sustaining presence in our lives. The name Rhianna carries the meaning “Majestic stream, shining brightly” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rhianna usually hope their child will grow to embody majestic stream, shining brightly and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the spiritual power and grace present in the natural world.
data.etymology: Rhianna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Majestic stream, shining brightly.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rhianna total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

modern_usage.modern_context: Rhianna is a common name for women in the modern world, particularly in the English-speaking world. It is derived from the Greek name Rhiannon, which means 'queen' or 'maiden'. In modern times, the name has been popularized by the singer Rihanna, who was born Robyn Rihanna Fenty in 1988. Rhianna's music career began in 2005, and she has since become one of the best-selling artists of all time. Her fashion sense has also been influential, particularly in the areas of makeup and hairstyles. Social media platforms such as Instagram and Twitter have played a significant role in the spread of the name Rhianna, as fans and admirers use these platforms to share images and information related to the singer and her music.
